text:
kevin: Heads-up — hit a weird latency storm from the Python SDK this morning after increasing idle_timeout on the AsyncClient pool.
kevin: Saw 500ms -> 3s tail latencies for short chat requests.
kevin: Repro steps: ramp traffic down to 0, wait 90s (idle_timeout set to 60), then burst 200 req/s.
maria: that smells like a thundering herd when connections are re-created. did you enable keepalive on the backend LB?
kevin: yes LB keepalive is on. stack shows many tcp connect attempts and SYN retransmits.
kevin: logs:
```
2026-03-18T09:41:02Z WARN httpx._transports.auto - connection failed: [Errno 110] Connection timed out
2026-03-18T09:41:02Z INFO devex.metrics - conn_pool.size=0 conn_opening=195 in_flight=5
```
jonah: can you paste your client config? might be our pool drain logic closing sockets too eagerly.
kevin: config snippet:
```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
c = AsyncClient(api_key=..., max_connections=100, idle_timeout=60, connection_retries=3)
```
kevin: also running uvloop, Python 3.11.
tara: hmm max_connections=100 and then 0 after idle purge, then burst creates N new connects concurrently -> should add jitter and staggered warmup.
maria: agreed. SDK should support staggered reconnect/backoff for pool warmups. also we don't surface an option to pre-warm N connections on demand.
kevin: repro script attached (short):
```
# ramp down then burst
await asyncio.sleep(70)
await gather([client.chat.generate(...) for _ in range(200)])
```
jonah: thanks. I can repro locally with the script. failing path seems to be async session drain + immediate recreate without limit.
jonah: proposed fixes:
- add randomized backoff when opening new connections in bulk
- ability to prefill pool with min_connections
- change idle drain to do rolling close (N at a time) instead of all-at-once
tara: backend infra can also accept connections slower; staggering will help.
kevin: +1 for min_connections API and a 'prefill' helper.
maria: also file-level typing: our AsyncClient type signature doesn't expose the pool tuning knobs in stubs; users miss them in autocomplete. ticket?
jonah: will open two PRs: one for runtime behavior (backoff/prefill) and one for typing/pyi updates.
ci-bot: Test run for PR #482: failing on flakey test test_pool_reconnect_race (timeout)
jonah: saw that — tests are non-deterministic because they assert exact connection counts. will update to assert within range and add timing buffer.
kevin: for immediate mitigation, can we add docs note: recommend idle_timeout >= expected quiesce + warmup and set max_connections conservative for bursty flows.
maria: also we've had a customer-reported Production incident with similar pattern last month; we should surface a sample app showing "burst-aware" client config.
tara: assigning to @jonah for code changes and @maria for docs + sample app. can we target a patch release this week?
jonah: I can target Tuesday patch. will include a small integration test to simulate burst after idle.
kevin: i'll sanity-run on staging tomorrow AM.
maria: created ISSUE-DEVEX-719 in tracker with steps, logs, and mitigation notes.
kevin: thanks. one more ask: add an opt-in env var REDWOOD_SDK_POOL_PREFILL to let ops pre-warm existing deployments easily.
jonah: okay will add env var and CLI flag for the prefill helper.
maria: leaving a note to add an example to the 'onboarding/examples/burst_handling.py' doc.
kevin: 👍 :rocket:
devex-bot: Reminder: please update CHANGELOG and add migration note for new config knobs.
kevin: pinging infra to check LB connection limits — @tara can you follow up?
tara: on it, I'll check with infra and post results in this thread.
maria: excellent, thanks all. keeping this thread as the single source for triage.
